Petition
 Through: Mr. Ravi Gupta, Sr. Adv. with 
 Akhil Sachar, Ms. Sumanda Tuls
 and Ms. Muskan, Advs.
 versus
 Delhi Development Authority & Anr. .....

Respondents
 Through: Ms. Shobhana Takiar, Sc for Dd
 Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, Sc fo
 with Mr. Sunil Kumar Jha and M
 Ms Akhtar, Advs. for R-2/Lac.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vikas Mahajan
 Order
% 03.09.2025 CM APPL. 55750/2025 (for interim relief)

1. The present application has been filed seeking following relief:
"a) Pass an interim order restraining the Respondents from initiating demolition and from taking over the possession of the land ad measuring 1282 square yards, out of Khasra No. 52/5, situated at Village Prahladpur Banger Industrial area in Village Prahladpur Banger till the disposal of the Petition;"
2.

Mr. Ravi Gupta, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners invites attention of the Court to the Kabza Karvai (possession proceedings), more particularly to page 57 of the paperbook, to contend that the possession of the property in question measuring 01 bigha and 04 biswas along with various other parcels of land was not taken for the reason that the said land was built up.
It is further observed in the said possession proceedings that the possession will be taken after demolition.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/09/2025 at 22:54:43 3.
He submits that no demolition has been carried out till date, therefore, the possession of the property in question has not been taken at any point of time.

sentences.text: He further invites attention of the Court to the award no. 14/2002-03, dated 08.07.2002 particularly the observation of the Land Acquisition Collector with regard to the interest payable under Section 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short 'the Act').

The said observation reads thus:
"In view of the absence of any documentary evidence on record to the contrary, I fixed Rs. 12.16 lakhs per acre to be the most reasonable price as on 01-04-2000.
The notification under section 4 was issued on 27-10-99 and the price of the land is to be determined as on the date of notification under section 4 itself.

I, accordingly,
determine the market value of the land @ Rs. 12.16 lakhs per acre or Rs. 253333.33 per bigha.

INTEREST :-
Interest U/S 34 of LA Act will be given on market value + solatium + additional amount as per judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court of. India @ 9% per annum from the date of taking over the possession till the payment of compensation."
(emphasis supplied)

5. Referring to the above quoted paragraph from the award, Mr. Gupta submits that it has been observed that interest @ 9% per annum shall be payable on the market value of the acquired land +
solatium + additional amount as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court from the date of taking over the possession till the payment of compensation.

6. He submits that since the possession was not taken over, therefore, there was no occasion for the Land Acquisition Collector to have calculated the interest payable to the land owner, therefore, the submission of the respondent no.1/DDA that the compensation has been paid to the original owners i.e. predecessors-in-interest of the present petitioner is misconceived.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/09/2025 at 22:54:43 7.

Elaborating further he submits that since the interest could not have been calculated till the time possession was taken over, therefore, the amount of compensation mentioned at serial no.489 against the name of the Bhim Singh (the original owner of the property) could not have been calculated especially with regard to the land, the possession of which was not taken.
8. Referring to Section 16 of the Act, he submits that it is only after the possession is taken that the land vests in the government.
Since the possession of the land in question, was admittedly not taken, as is evident from the proceedings of the possession, therefore, the land does not vest either in the government or in the DDA.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Gupta further invites attention of the Court to the judgment of the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court in Sunil Goel & Ors. vs. State, 2014 SCC OnLine Del 2771 , to contend that the declaration under Section 6 qua the land in question was declared nullity.

entities.text: Sunil Goel & Ors. vs. State, 2014 SCC OnLine Del 2771
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the said decision is a judgment in rem and will apply to the case of the present petitioner as well.
10. In view of the above, issue notice.
Ms. Shobhana Takiar, learned Standing Counsel for the respondent/DDA accepts notice.
Likewise, Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, learned Standing Counsel for the respondent no.2 accepts notice.
11. Ms. Takiar submits that the petitioner is only a GPA holder and does not have any title to the property in question.
12. She further contends that the compensation has already been paid, and the memorandum of the possession tantamount to taking of possession of the acquired land.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/09/2025 at 22:54:43 13.
She further contends that the GPA on the basis of which the petitioner is claiming right over the land is of the year 2009 whereas the award is of the year 2002.

14. This Court finds that the notice was issued by this Court vide order dated 04.07.2025 and two weeks' time was granted to the respondent no.1/DDA to file counter-affidavit but the same has not been filed.
15. Having regard to the rival contention of the parties, this Court is of the view that the issues raised by Mr. Gupta requires consideration.
Accordingly, it is directed that the parties shall maintain status quo till the next date.

16. Let counter-affidavit be filed before the next date.
17. List on 15.09.2025, the date already fixed.
18.
Order dasti under the Signatures of the Court Master.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J SEPTEMBER 3, 2025/
